items.text: BusinessToday (1 day ago) confirmed: Sensex +941 to 77,958. Nifty +298 to 24,330. BSE market cap Rs 472.81 lakh crore. NBC News confirmed: Brent closed -7.8% at $101.27. WTI -7% at $95.08. US crude plunged as much as 15% to $88 intraday — the largest single-session crude fall in years — before recovering to close at $95.08. The trigger: White House sources told Axios the US believes it is nearing a one-page 14-point MOU. But Trump told the New York Post it was "too soon" to prepare to sign — causing prices to recover from lows. Net result: massive volatility, oil closes down 7-8% but well off the intraday crash lows.

items.bold: TRUMP (NY Post): "Too soon" to sign deal. Threatens: "Bombing starts at MUCH HIGHER LEVEL and intensity than before."
items.text: NBC News confirmed: Trump told the New York Post in an interview that it was "too soon" to prepare to sign a peace deal — causing oil to recover from the $88 intraday low. Trump also posted on Truth Social: "If they don't agree, the bombing starts, and it will be, sadly, at a much higher level and intensity than it was before." The threat is explicit: accept the MOU framework or face resumed airstrikes far more intensive than February 28's Operation Epic Fury. Trump also said that if a deal is agreed, the US naval blockade of Iranian ports would "allow the Hormuz Strait to be OPEN TO ALL, including Iran." This framing — open to Iran too — signals the US is prepared to fully lift the blockade as part of a deal, removing a key Iranian demand.

items.bold: VANCE, WITKOFF, KUSHNER held IN-PERSON TALKS in ISLAMABAD. Iran Navy: "new protocols" for Hormuz passage.
items.text: NBC News confirmed: Vice President JD Vance, special envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner held in-person talks in the Pakistani capital, Islamabad — the most senior US diplomatic delegation to Pakistan since the war began. Pakistan is the primary intermediary between the US and Iran. The in-person talks signal the US is treating the next few days as the decisive window for a deal. Separately: Iran's navy said Wednesday that "with aggressor's threats neutralized and new protocols in place, safe, stable passage through the Strait of Hormuz will be ensured." This ambiguous statement could signal either a deal framework or Iran's toll/protocol system — unclear. On Wednesday, zero ships crossed Hormuz (S&P Global). On Tuesday, only one ship crossed.

items.bold: BRENT FELL BELOW $100 Thursday — $99.40 (-1.85%). FIRST TIME below $100 since the war began.
items.text: CNBC (2 hours ago) confirmed: Brent crude fell 1.85% to $99.40 per barrel Thursday — falling below the $100 psychological threshold for the first time since the war began on February 28. WTI rose 1.85% to $93.21 per barrel (some intraday volatility). Business Standard (3 hours ago) confirmed Brent slipped below $100 on Thursday with Nifty settling below 24,350. For India: Brent below $100 is the first time the war's oil shock has eased below this critical level. At $99.40: the OMC petrol/diesel hike is virtually off the table. Rupee is strengthening. Gulf fertiliser sourcing is becoming commercially viable again. India's import bill is improving rapidly from the $126 peak.

items.bold: IRAN FM BAQAEI: Tehran reviewing US proposal — response to Pakistan mediators coming. Murkowski AUMF May 11.
items.text: CNBC (2 hours ago) confirmed: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said Wednesday that Tehran is still reviewing the proposal and would present its response to mediators in Pakistan. Baqaei appeared to cite the International Court of Justice, writing that "the concept of negotiations requires, at the very least, a genuine attempt to engage in discussions." This signals Iran is engaging diplomatically but carefully — not accepting and not rejecting. The response to Pakistan mediators is the next critical milestone. Separately: Senator Murkowski's AUMF deadline is May 11 — Senate returns this week. If the WH has no credible plan, a formal war authorization vote is forced. This congressional pressure is another driver pushing the White House toward a deal this week.

Trump also posted: "If they don't agree, the bombing starts, and it will be, sadly, at a much higher level and intensity than it was before." military.t: ZERO Ships Crossed Hormuz Wednesday. Iran Navy: "New Protocols — Safe Passage Ensured."
military.d: NBC News and S&P Global Market Intelligence confirmed: Zero ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday. On Tuesday, only one ship crossed. This is the lowest shipping traffic since the war began — even lower than the days immediately after February 28 closure. Iran's navy said Wednesday that "with aggressor's threats neutralized and new protocols in place, safe, stable passage through the Strait of Hormuz will be ensured." The "new protocols" language is ambiguous — it could reference Iran's toll/coordination system, or a deal-adjacent framework. Former US Ambassador to Oman Marc Sievers (CNBC): "The immediate focus has been on a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz — no toll imposed by the Iranian IRGC on tankers to pass." ING: 23,000 seafarers across 87 countries stranded.

military.t: IRAN FM BAQAEI: Response to Pakistan Mediators Coming. Murkowski AUMF May 11 Pressure.
military.d: CNBC (2 hours ago) confirmed: Iranian FM spokesperson Baqaei said Tehran is still reviewing the proposal and would present its response to mediators in Pakistan. Baqaei cited the International Court of Justice on what "negotiations" require — signalling Iran is engaging carefully but not accepting outright. Iran also stated it will "only accept a fair and comprehensive agreement." The response to Pakistan mediators is the next critical milestone — expected Friday-Saturday. Separately: Murkowski AUMF deadline May 11 creates congressional pressure on the WH to show a credible plan. If Murkowski introduces AUMF: forces Senate to vote on formally authorising or ending the war — removing Trump's executive flexibility.

assessment.body:
Thursday 7 PM IST. Day 69. Brent is below $100 for the first time since the war began.

THE WEDNESDAY FINAL PICTURE
• Sensex +941 to 77,958. Nifty +298 to 24,330. BSE market cap Rs 472.81 lakh crore
• Brent closed $101.27 (-7.8%). WTI $95.08 (-7%). WTI plunged to $88 intraday (-15%)
• Trump (NY Post): "too soon" to sign deal — prices recovered from lows
• Trump: "If they don't agree, the bombing starts at much higher level and intensity than before"
• Iran navy: "with new protocols in place, safe stable passage will be ensured"
• ZERO ships crossed Hormuz Wednesday (S&P Global). One crossed Tuesday.
• Vance, Witkoff, Kushner held in-person talks in Islamabad (NBC News)
• 23,000 seafarers across 87 countries stranded

THURSDAY — BRENT BELOW $100
• Brent fell 1.85% to $99.40 — first time below $100 since February 28
• WTI $93.21. Market pricing significant deal probability
• Nifty settled below 24,350 — flat, marginal losses. Derivatives expiry volatility
• Auto, Realty, Chemical buying. IT, Consumer Durables, FMCG declining
• Iran FM Baqaei: response to Pakistan mediators coming (expected Friday-Saturday)
• Murkowski AUMF May 11 — Senate returns this week

THE ISLAMABAD TALKS — WHY THEY MATTER
• Vance (VP) + Witkoff (senior envoy) + Kushner (son-in-law) = most senior US delegation since war began
• Pakistan is the primary mediator between US and Iran
• In-person presence signals the US treats next 48-72 hours as decisive
• Iran FM Baqaei response to Pakistan expected Friday-Saturday
• Former US Ambassador Sievers (CNBC): focus is full reopening, no Iranian IRGC toll

THE INDIA MOMENT
• Brent $99.40 = OMC hike virtually off table — biggest relief since the war began
• Rupee strengthening rapidly from ATL 95.32 toward Rs 93.50-94
• Kharif fertiliser: at Brent $99, Gulf imports commercially viable — restart sourcing NOW
• June planting window: May 11-15 is the critical restart period
• Nifty flat Thursday = market waiting for Iran FM response
• If MOU signed this weekend: Sensex 86,000+, rupee Rs 91-92, Brent $78-82

VERDICT: Day 69 closes with the West Asia War at its most decisive moment since February 28. Brent is below $100 for the first time. The US VP is in Islamabad. Iran is preparing its response. Trump has issued both a deal signal ("open to all including Iran") and a bombing threat ("much higher level and intensity"). The next 48-72 hours — from Friday through Sunday — will determine whether the 69-day energy crisis that has cost India Rs 50+ trillion in economic value begins its end, or enters its most dangerous phase.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
